summary: This note is the documentation page for Snowflake's TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS Account Usage view, which reports table-level storage utilization used to calculate per-table storage billing, including dropped tables still incurring storage costs. It breaks billed bytes into active, Time Travel, Fail-safe, and retained-for-clone categories, lists the view's columns with descriptions, and gives usage notes on latency, ID and clone group behavior, dropped tables, and zero-day Time Travel retention.
one_line: Snowflake Account Usage view reporting per-table storage bytes (active, Time Travel, Fail-safe, clone-retained) used for storage billing.
key_facts: The TABLE_STORAGE_METRICS view is an Account Usage view that displays table-level storage utilization used to calculate storage billing for each table in the account.
The view includes tables that have been dropped but are still incurring storage costs.
Snowflake breaks billed bytes into active bytes and deleted bytes, and deleted bytes are sub-categorized into Time Travel, Fail-safe, and bytes retained for clones.
ACTIVE_BYTES is bytes owned by and billed to the table that are in the active state, representing data that can be queried.
TIME_TRAVEL_BYTES covers bytes still within the Time Travel retention period for the table, meaning recently deleted data.
FAILSAFE_BYTES covers deleted bytes past the Time Travel retention period but within the Fail-safe period for the table.
RETAINED_FOR_CLONE_BYTES covers deleted bytes no longer in Time Travel or Fail-safe that are still retained because clones of the table reference them.
CLONE_GROUP_ID is the unique identifier for the oldest clone ancestor of a table and is the same as ID if the table is not a clone.
IS_TRANSIENT is 'YES' if the table is transient or temporary, and transient and temporary tables have no Fail-safe period.
The DELETED column is TRUE if the table has been purged from storage.
Dropped tables in Fail-safe (TABLE_ENTERED_FAILSAFE is not NULL) will potentially display NULL values in most columns, and these tables cannot be restored using UNDROP.
Storage bytes are always owned by and billed to the table where the bytes were initially added, and cloned tables do not inherit those initial bytes' metrics.
Latency for the view may be up to 90 minutes.
When data is deleted from a table with a Time Travel retention period of 0 days, TIME_TRAVEL_BYTES may contain a non-zero value briefly while background processes complete.
Any data in the DELETED column prior to August 2018 may not be accurate.
